Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Obese adults with depression had significantly lower mean serum 25(OH)D than obese adults without depression.
Sentence: "The mean 25(OH) D levels were significantly different between depressed and non-depressed groups (20 ± 15 vs. 27 ± 13, P < 0.001)."
Measured as: depression (DSM-5 diagnosis)
Population: Obese adults aged 18-60 attending an outpatient obesity clinic in Tehran, Iran, with and without DSM-5 depression
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (observational exposure)
Comparator: Obese adults without depression
Design: case-control study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation at baseline was not associated with depression at 2.5 years in people with multiple sclerosis.
Sentence: "Vitamin D supplementation and meditation were not associated with outcomes."
Measured as: depression
Population: People with multiple sclerosis from the HOLISM study who completed baseline and 2.5-year follow-up surveys
Intervention: Vitamin D supplementation (self-reported, assessed at baseline)
Comparator: No vitamin D supplementation
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 1,401
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"evaluation":"All three responses reach the same verdict and primary reason (genuine, population), which is defensible: an observational serum-level association in obese Iranian adults versus a null supplementation cohort in MS. Arguably design_or_bias is the more fitting primary reason, since the rules treat an observational association against a null study as design-driven, but population is plausible given the distinct clinical groups. The responses differ mainly in the quality of detail and also_differs. Response A gives the most informative detail (case-control on serum level vs MS cohort, self-reported supplementation, 2.5-year follow-up) and lists the broadest set of secondary differences, though its rationale says they 'do not clearly conflict' while still labelling the pair genuine, which is inconsistent. Response B is clean and consistent but its detail covers only population, repeating the primary reason. Response C omits outcome_measure and its rationale is thinnest, though its detail does capture the exposure contrast. Note that all three use 'rationale' instead of 'evaluation' structure aside, so I rank on substantive quality.","ranking":["A","C","B","D","E","F","G","H"]}
